extracted.intended_audience: WHO communicators and public health communication professionals (country, regional, and headquarters offices)
extracted.subtask_description: A strategic framework for designing, producing, and evaluating WHO communications so they are actionable, accessible, relevant, timely, understandable and credible for health decision‑makers and other key audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Make information available online; identify effective channels; ensuring Accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make information available online and identify effective channels that reach target audiences. Ensure accessibility (e.g., formats, platforms and other measures to make content reachable and usable by people with different needs). Use tactics and planning questions to design communications that are accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Know the audience; listen to the audience; tailor the message; motivate the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand and research the audience so messages are tailored to their needs and contexts. Actively listen to audience feedback and adapt content. Design messages that motivate the intended audience to consider or adopt recommended actions. Relevance is judged by how well content aligns with audience needs and decision contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable
rubrics_metrics.description: Move audiences to action; behaviour change campaigns; communicate in emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should be designed to prompt specific, practicable actions by audiences. Use behaviour-change campaign techniques where appropriate and ensure emergency communications provide clear, actionable guidance. Tactics and planning questions should help translate guidance into concrete steps audiences can take.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate early; communicate at the right time; build the conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue messages early enough to influence decisions and at moments when audiences are receptive. Timing should enable two‑way engagement (‘build the conversation’) and sustained relevance across evolving situations. Plan communications schedules to maximize impact and responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credible
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical accuracy; be transparent; coordinate with partners; speak as 'One WHO'; WHO brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure technical accuracy and transparency in content. Coordinate messaging with partners and across WHO offices to present a unified voice ('One WHO') and maintain WHO brand integrity. Credibility is reinforced by clear sourcing, openness about uncertainties, and consistent coordination with stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understandable
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plain language; tell real stories; make it visual; use familiar languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present information in plain language and culturally familiar terms. Use storytelling, visuals, and translations into familiar languages to increase comprehension. Avoid jargon; use concrete examples and visual aids to make complex health information intelligible to non‑technical audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation is judging WHO messages, products, and engagements based on their effectiveness at reaching specified goals and principles (evaluation and assessment used synonymously).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should be applied at all levels to assess whether communications achieved intended goals and adhered to the framework principles. Use metrics and assessment methods to judge effectiveness, inform iterative improvements, and update tactics as audience needs and contexts change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal and key audiences (health decision‑makers)
rubrics_metrics.description: WHO communicates to and with key audiences - the agents who use WHO communications products to make a range of health decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and prioritise audiences as the health decision‑makers whose choices WHO communications are designed to inform or influence. Design messages, channels, and tactics around how these audiences use information to make decisions; ensure outputs are actionable and targeted to their decision contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated and coordinated communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective, integrated and coordinated communications are integral to achieving WHO’s goals and delivering its mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a strategic approach that integrates communications across issues, regions and functions. Use coordinated planning, shared tactics, and consistent messaging to amplify impact and reduce fragmentation. Coordination includes internal alignment (country, regional, HQ) and external partner engagement.
